title: Low-dose lung CT for smokers
what: A CT scan of the chest with a lower radiation dose. It looks for small changes in the lungs before you have any complaints.
why: Usually for older people who smoke a lot or used to. Your doctor decides whether you need it.
duration: the scan itself takes a few minutes, the report usually comes in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: How many years and how many cigarettes a day you smoke or smoked
If you recently had pneumonia or a cold
If you have had a lung CT before

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: No special preparation is needed. You can eat.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: No metal on your chest: take off chains and a bra with underwire.

prepare.title: Earlier scans
prepare.text: Bring earlier CT scans - the doctor needs to compare.

steps: You lie on your back on the scanner table, arms above your head
The table slides into the ring of the scanner
You are asked to breathe in and hold your breath
The scan takes a few seconds
The table slides out - and that is all
feel: The scanner is open, it is not a tight tube
after: The report is usually ready in 1 to 3 days
If small nodules are found, most often a follow-up scan is set after some time - the doctor decides

faq.q: If a nodule is found, is it cancer?
faq.a: Most often not. Most nodules are harmless. The doctor will tell you whether follow-up is needed.

faq.q: How often should it be done?
faq.a: Usually once a year, while there is a reason for it. The doctor decides.

faq.q: Will it help to quit smoking?
faq.a: Yes. It is the best thing for your lungs at any age.

reminders.text: Lung CT tomorrow. No preparation needed. Take earlier scans and wear clothes without metal.
